hints.content:
When a differential equation is in the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{f(x)}{g(y)}$ we can try to solve it by separation of variables.

For the equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{e^x}{y^2}$, we have:

$\begin{align}
f(x)&=e^x
\\\\
g(y)&=y^2
\end{align}$

Let's separate the variables.

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=\dfrac{f(x)}{g(y)}
\\\\
g(y)\,dy&=f(x)\,dx
\\\\
y^2\,dy&=e^x\,dx
\\\\
\displaystyle \int y^2\,dy&=\displaystyle \int e^x\,dx
\end{align}$

Baylee separated the variables correctly.

Let's integrate.

$\begin{align}
\displaystyle \int y^2\,dy&=\displaystyle \int e^x\,dx
\\\\
\dfrac{y^3}{3}&=e^x+C
\end{align}$

Baylee forgot to add $C$ immediately to represent the information lost between a function and its derivative. It is not equivalent to wait until the end of isolating $y$ and then to add $C$.
In conclusion, step 2 is incorrect. The right-hand side of the equation should be $e^x+C$.

question.content:
Baylee tried to solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{e^x}{y^2}$. This is her work:

$\begin{align}
&&\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=\dfrac{e^x}{y^2}
\\\\
\text{Step 1:}&&\displaystyle\int y^2\,dy&=\displaystyle\int e^x\,dx
\\\\
\text{Step 2:}&&\dfrac{y^3}{3}&=e^x
\\\\
\text{Step 3:}&&y^3&=3e^x
\\\\
\text{Step 4:}&&y&=\sqrt[3]{3e^x}+C
\end{align}$

**Is Baylee's work correct? If not, what is her mistake?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: When Baylee integrates, she needs to add a constant to the right side of the equation immediately.  It is not equivalent to wait until the end of the algebraic manipulations, then add the constant.

$\begin{align}
f(x)&=e^x
\\\\
g(y)&=y^2
\\\\
\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=\dfrac{f(x)}{g(y)}
\\\\
g(y)\,dy&=f(x)\,dx
\\\\
y^2\,dy&=e^x\,dx
\\\\
\displaystyle \int y^2\,dy&=\displaystyle \int e^x\,dx
\end{align}$
choices.content: **Step 1** is incorrect. The separation of variables wasn't done correctly.

choices.clue: When Baylee integrates, she needs to add a constant to the right side of the equation immediately.  It is not equivalent to wait until the end of the algebraic manipulations, then add the constant.
choices.content: **Step 2** is incorrect. The right-hand side of the equation should be $e^x+C$.

choices.clue: While the cube root should apply to the constant as well to $3e^x$, both terms should be within the same root. $\sqrt[3]{a}+\sqrt[3]{b} \neq \sqrt[3]{a+b}$
choices.content: **Step 4** is incorrect. The right-hand side of the equation should be $\sqrt[3]{3e^x}+\sqrt[3]{C}$.
